head: Regulation of kidney development
name: Regulation of kidney development (kidney size restraint, nephric duct and ureter, mesenchyme survival)
rationale: All members regulate kidney development, and the restraint of growth and size, nephric duct-ureter morphogenesis and mesenchymal anti-apoptosis separate it from the ureteric bud and metanephric differentiation confusables.

head: Reelin signalling in synapse maturation
name: Reelin signalling in synapse maturation (dendritic spines, dendrite development, long-term depression)
rationale: Reelin signalling drives dendrite, spine and synapse maturation and plasticity, which separates it from the amyloid-beta and actin-based postsynaptic structure confusables.

head: Glucogenic amino acid metabolism and gluconeogenesis
name: Glucogenic amino acid metabolism and gluconeogenesis (glutamate and glutamine, aspartate, alanine)
rationale: Glutamate, glutamine, aspartate and alanine metabolism feed carbon via oxaloacetate into gluconeogenesis, distinguishing it from the proline/glycine, TCA cycle and conjugation confusables.

head: Sphingolipid metabolism
name: Sphingolipid metabolism (ceramide, sphingomyelin)
rationale: Members cover sphingolipid synthesis, breakdown and homeostasis centred on ceramide and sphingomyelin, unlike the glycerophospholipid confusables.

head: Lipoprotein particle remodeling
name: Lipoprotein particle remodeling (HDL, LDL)
rationale: All members are remodeling of HDL and LDL particles, which separates it from the chylomicron and VLDL assembly and clearance confusables.

head: Mitochondrial gene expression and genome maintenance
name: Mitochondrial gene expression and genome maintenance (mtDNA replication, mRNA turnover, mitoribosome translation)
rationale: Members span mitochondrial DNA replication and repair, transcription, mRNA stability and mitoribosome translation, whereas the confusables add tRNA processing and RNA import.

head: Neuropeptide signalling in sleep-wake regulation
name: Neuropeptide signalling in sleep-wake regulation (opioid receptors, orexin, dense-core vesicle release)
rationale: Neuropeptide and opioid GPCR signalling released from dense-core vesicles, chiefly controlling sleep and wakefulness, distinguishes it from the stress-hormone and social/mating behaviour confusables.

head: Response to replication-blocking DNA damage
name: Response to replication-blocking DNA damage (protein-DNA crosslinks, camptothecin, hydroxyurea)
rationale: Protein-DNA crosslink repair and responses to camptothecin and hydroxyurea all deal with lesions that stall replication, unlike the Fanconi, double-strand break and fork-reversal confusables.

head: Inflammatory monocyte recruitment and activation
name: Inflammatory monocyte recruitment and activation (chemotaxis and extravasation, aggregation, proinflammatory cytokines)
rationale: Members describe monocyte activation, aggregation and migration into inflamed tissue together with the inflammatory cytokine response, which separates it from monocyte surface-signature and anti-inflammatory confusables.

head: Intrinsic pathway coagulation
name: Intrinsic pathway coagulation (defective factor VIII, defective factor IX)
rationale: Members are the intrinsic coagulation pathway and its factor VIII and IX variant defects, distinguishing it from the factor XII, von Willebrand factor, factor V and fibrinolysis confusables.

head: Endothelial specification and vascular morphogenesis
name: Endothelial specification and vascular morphogenesis (VEGFR2, Tie2, arterial-venous-lymphatic fate)
rationale: Members cover endothelial fate commitment and vessel formation driven by VEGFR2 and Tie2 signalling, unlike the sprouting-angiogenesis and BMP-driven cardiac vessel confusables.

head: Cardiomyocyte calcium homeostasis
name: Cardiomyocyte calcium homeostasis (sodium-calcium exchange, cytosolic calcium clearance)
rationale: Members control cardiac calcium handling with emphasis on sodium-calcium exchange lowering cytosolic calcium, which the SR pump, ryanodine-receptor and caffeine-response confusables lack.

head: Damaged-protein repair under cellular stress
name: Damaged-protein repair under cellular stress (methylglyoxal glycation, nitrosative stress, chaperone-mediated autophagy)
rationale: Members protect and repair proteins under stress, with methylglyoxal handling and protein repair distinguishing it from the aggrephagy, heat-shock and ROS detoxification confusables.

head: Hindbrain branchiomotor neuron development
name: Hindbrain branchiomotor neuron development (tangential migration, facial nerve, trigeminal nerve)
rationale: Branchiomotor neuron migration and axon guidance build the facial and trigeminal nerves, unlike the brainstem maturation, cerebellar and sensory placode confusables.

head: Differentiated intestinal epithelium identity
name: Differentiated intestinal epithelium identity (CDX and HNF4 factors, enterocytes, barrier maintenance)
rationale: Members mark the CDX/HNF4-specified differentiated absorptive gut epithelium and its barrier, distinguishing it from the crypt stem cell, antimicrobial and pancreatic lineage confusables.

head: Chemokine receptor-driven leukocyte chemotaxis
name: Chemokine receptor-driven leukocyte chemotaxis (dendritic cells, T and NK cells, CCR7 and CXCR4)
rationale: Chemokine receptor signalling directs dendritic cell, T cell and NK cell migration, which separates it from the integrin, B cell homing and monocyte confusables.

head: Amino acid and oligopeptide transport
name: Amino acid and oligopeptide transport (proton-coupled oligopeptide cotransport, cationic amino acids)
rationale: Members move amino acids and di/oligopeptides across membranes, and proton-coupled peptide transport and cationic amino acid import distinguish it from the neutral amino acid, polyamine and ornithine confusables.

head: Epithelial cell migration control
name: Epithelial cell migration control (reduced cell-matrix adhesion, Rho and Rac inhibition, keratinocytes)
rationale: Members tune epithelial and keratinocyte migration by suppressing matrix adhesion, spreading and Rho/Rac-driven protrusion, unlike the CDC42/actin-polymerization and VEGF confusables.

head: Double-strand break sensing and repair choice
name: Double-strand break sensing and repair choice (NHEJ, ATM signalling, BRCA1 and BRCA2 defects)
rationale: Members sense breaks, signal via ATM and choose between NHEJ and homologous recombination including BRCA1/BRCA2 defects, distinguishing it from the PARylation and resection/HR-execution confusables.

head: Golgi nucleotide-sugar transport
name: Golgi nucleotide-sugar transport (SLC35 transporter defects, congenital glycosylation disorders, UDP-glucuronate)
rationale: Members supply nucleotide sugars to the Golgi lumen and include transporter defects causing glycosylation disorders, unlike the GPI, glycosphingolipid, sialic acid and N-glycan confusables.

head: Hematopoietic interleukin receptor signalling
name: Hematopoietic interleukin receptor signalling (IL-2/7/9, IL-3/5, STAT5)
rationale: Members are common gamma-chain and beta-common interleukin receptor signalling through STAT5, with the IL-3/IL-5 arm separating it from the IL-15/21 T cell, IL-6 and FLT3 confusables.

head: Purine ribonucleotide catabolism
name: Purine ribonucleotide catabolism (AMP and IMP, ADA and PNP defects, allantoin)
rationale: Members degrade purine ribonucleotides and nucleosides via inosine towards allantoin, unlike the salvage and deoxyribonucleotide confusables.

head: Chemosensory perception
name: Chemosensory perception (smell, sour taste)
rationale: Members are chemical sensing by smell and sour taste, distinguishing it from olfactory receptor expression, acid-sensing channel and sweet/bitter/umami taste confusables.

head: AP-1 immediate-early gene response
name: AP-1 immediate-early gene response (UV, nitric oxide, mitogens and phorbol ester)
rationale: AP-1/FOS-driven immediate-early transcription in response to UV, nitric oxide and mitogenic stimuli distinguishes it from the TAK1-JNK/p38 kinase and ERK feedback confusables.

head: Regulation of nucleocytoplasmic protein transport
name: Regulation of nucleocytoplasmic protein transport (nuclear import, nuclear export)
rationale: Members regulate protein import into and export from the nucleus, unlike the nuclear pore assembly and RNA/inositol phosphate transport confusables.
